newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - off about 3/8, quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - off about 3/8, quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were off 3/8 in the cash market, following declines in the U.S. Treasury market caused by a robust GDP number.

The U.S. Commerce Department reported at 0830 EDT on Wednesday that real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew at an annual rate of 5.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997, a nine-year high, after an increase of 3.8 percent in the final estimate of the fourth quarter 1996.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected, on average, a 4.1 percent rise in the first quarter.

The benchmark 30-year bond in the wake of the report was off 19/32 at 94-29/32 to yield 7.03 percent, giving up some of the gains made on Tuesday. But the long bond regained some ground, moving off 12/32 at 95-4/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
Municipal traders said munis were following the Treasury market, but that the price erosion was not as bad.
"We have not lost that much," one trader said.
Traders noted that some bid lists were out, but nothing substantial.

Also on Tuesday, munis had garnered about one point on the Employment Cost Index report that in the first quarter the index only rose 0.6 percent--less than 0.9 percent predicted in a Reuters consensus suvery of economists.

June municipal bond futures regained some ground from the early morning but were down 5 ticks to 113-25/32, while June Treasury bonds were down 11 ticks at 108-19/32. This left the MOB spread at 166 ticks, widening from the close of 160 ticks on Tuesday.
Over in the primary market, municipal bond sales for Wednesday are expected to total $445 million in 18 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $389 million in 10 sales, with a $155 million Lorain County, Ohio deal through Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc., topping the list.
On the competitive side, eight sales totaling $60 million are on the schedule. A $17 million Kent County, Mich., deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
An additional two sales totaling $37 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds Wednesday, depending on market conditions.
